modelingNotes: Academy Museum of Motion Pictures, Wilshire Blvd at Fairfax, Los Angeles: the Saban Building (former May Company, Albert C. Martin and Samuel Marx, 1939) and Renzo Piano's sphere (David Geffen Theater, 2021) behind it, linked by glass bridges — one model for both. Original procedural geometry, CC0-1.0. bun generators/la-academy-museum.ts [out.glb]

Map frame before placement: u along Wilshire (east), v toward the north, z up, metres; origin at the area centroid of the Saban outline (way/426357430: -118.3607923, 34.0632679), on the ground (flat, 3DEP and lidar ~50.8 m). Placed at bearing 7.8°, Wilshire's rotation here.

Identity: the pale limestone box with the gold-tiled cylinder on the Wilshire/Fairfax corner, framed by tall black granite slabs; the black granite base; and the sphere, concrete below and a glass dome above.

Plan: OSM way/426357430 (Saban, 3,862 m2; height 34.8), way/1360732450 (Sphere Building, height 39.6) with its parts 1360732451 (dome, a circle ~42.6 m across), 913293589, 1113417080 (the base between the sphere and the Saban) and 1113417081.

Heights: LA County lidar DSM (LARIAC, 2.5 m grid, sampled 2026): ground 50.8 m; Saban south range 23.5 m, north range 28 m, central penthouse 34 m; the corner frame ~29 m; a 5–8 m canopy at the corner. The lidar predates the sphere; its 39.6 m is OSM's height.

Photos (Wikimedia Commons): a5 "The May Company Building 2021" (Downtowngal, CC BY-SA 4.0; the corner from the south-west across Wilshire/Fairfax: gold cylinder, black frame, window rows, black base); a6 "Academy Museum (51378465751)" (Eden, Janine and Jim, CC BY 2.0; corner from the south-east); a1 "The Sphere Academy Museum 2021" and a2 "Sphere of the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures" (Downtowngal, CC BY-SA 4.0; the sphere from the north-west and north-east: concrete lower half, glass dome, bridges and stair tower to the Saban); a3 "Academy Museum of Motion Pictures (February 2025)" (Fred Cherrygarden, CC BY-SA 4.0; the glazed north face and a bridge).

Estimated: the cylinder (7.7 m radius, on the outline's rounded corner) and the frame slabs (a5), the window panels (one per bay, two floors tall, after a5's rows), the sphere's centre height (radius 21 m from OSM, top at 39.6 m, so it sinks a little into the ground as it seems to behind the fence in a2), the glass dome starting just above the equator, the bridges' levels (a1). Left out: the stair tower, the ACADEMY MUSEUM lettering on the frame, the gold tiles' banding, the sphere's panel joints and the dome's steel grid.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "la-academy-museum", model "la-academy-museum"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/la-academy-museum.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
Window panels clipped to the walls behind them; 138 m² of glazing with no wall behind it (curtain walls, glazing past a wall's edge) uses the la-academy-museum-glazing finish in the window colour.
To fit six materials, folded la-academy-museum-glass into la-academy-museum-academy-concrete (ΔE 9.7).
